function.arguments: {"reason": "The sentinel values (-999.0) in biomarker_baseline represent missing data and were unevenly distributed by sex (43 in females, 50 in males). This introduced a potential confounding bias because baseline biomarker levels are predictive of response. After removing these rows, the sex distribution remained slightly imbalanced (51.1% male, 48.9% female), but the key confounder—arm assignment—was also imbalanced (63% control, 37% treatment). The raw response rate difference (0.688 vs 0.671) persisted, but the difference was not consistent across arms: females responded better in the control arm (74.7% vs 68.8%) but worse in the treatment arm (59.3% vs 64.0%). This suggests the overall difference is due to confounding by arm, not sex itself. Thus, the original question 'Why do female patients respond better?' is based on a confounded comparison. The correct interpretation is that the observed difference is not causal but due to systematic differences in arm assignment. The question cannot be answered as asked because the premise is confounded."}
function.name: resolve_finding
